column4: member insertion into an existing type is a new row kind (MERGE), not a FILE copy: the donor type's body goes between two anchors before the host's closing brace, the donor imports the host lacks are inserted at their sorted position, and the donor header/package/type Javadoc/type line are structural, not copied; the host is pinned (BASE row, host_sha256 = target minus block minus recipe imports) so a re-run proves the host bytes are still the planned master file
column5: PROVENANCE.tsv base_match=TRUE for the Java and the C host; --check changed=0 provenance=UNCHANGED

column4: idempotent bookkeeping of the merge needs the recipe's own state: the imports it inserted are recorded per target (inserted_imports, as fully qualified names) and read back on the next run to recompute the host pin; storing the whole import line broke on the ";" separator of the TSV cell, and the blank line the recipe puts before its begin anchor belongs to the block (strip_block takes it), or the host pin drifts by one line per run
column5: second run before the fix: base_match=FALSE provenance=CHANGED; after: base_match=TRUE, --check exit 0

column4: the donor's loader harness (System.load of a property path, NATIVE_LOADED flag, private constructor) is not product code of the host: declared DROP_LINE/DROP_METHOD rows remove it (11 lines), one REWRITE row maps NATIVE_LOADED to the host-pattern lazy holder NativeLaneKernel.AVAILABLE (library loaded AND laneKernelAbiNative() == 1), one INSERT_BLOCK row per file adds the holder and its C probe in the host's own ABI-probe shape (its 6th instance); every other donor body line is byte for byte (body_match=TRUE), and the proof's native branches run through the module library
